content:
Black Friday is once again upon us, offering a ridiculous amount of deals on physical movies and TV shows. One such deal is The Legend of Zelda: The Complete Series on DVD, which is back down to $8.99 on Amazon. The Black Friday discounts knocks 55% off the sticker price of $19.98, matching the lowest-ever price we've seen on the DVD.

The single-disc DVD release includes all 13 episodes of The Legend of Zelda animated series that ran throughout 1989. Unfortunately, it doesn't come come any other special features, commentaries, or extras.

The series, which was produced by now-defunct DIC Entertainment, loosely adapts the first two Zelda games from the NES era. It's not exactly canon, however, and is a bit of an odd swing from the early era of Zelda. Reviews aren't the most glowing, but it has a surprisingly dedicated cult following. At this price, there's no harm in having some fun with a silly series you might be curious about.

The DVD makes a great addition to any Zelda fan's collection or a fun gift for that special Hyrule lover in your life, especially with the winter holidays around the corner. It's also a good way to hold yourself over until The Legend of Zelda live-action movie comes out in early 2027, though I really hope whatever Sony and Nintendo end up doing is a bit higher quality than this.

Editor's Note: If you've never seen the series before, it's currently free to stream on Tubi. You should definitely give it a try before you think about actually buying the DVD.

Nintendo Is Going All Out for Black Friday

Nintendo's official Black Friday sale is now live, and it happens to include the only console deal of the year. Unfortunately that deal only includes the base model Nintendo Switch 2, but we're keeping an eye out for restocks and discounts on the special Zelda anniversary edition.

In the meantime, Nintendo is also offering tons of discounts on great digital games, including the recently released remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which earned a 9 out of 10 in our review by Logan Plant.

Even more physical games are on sale at retailers like Amazon and Walmart. If you're on the hunt for more than just gaming deals, check out our full hub of Black Friday madness.
